subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: What subagent breaker contract should OpenClaw core own: a first-class persisted session-health receipt, a narrow spawn-failure counter, or consolidation under the broader session-health breaker work?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested fix crosses config schema, persisted runtime state, failure taxonomy, cooldown/reset behavior, UI/CLI status, and overlap with adjacent breaker issues.

options.title: Design persisted session-health receipts
options.body: Define failure signature, counter scope, last success, cooldown or half-open state, manual override, notification, and status output before implementation.

options.title: Land a narrow spawn-failure breaker
options.body: Limit the first change to consecutive terminal subagent failures keyed by agent or task signature, leaving provider/session/UI semantics for follow-ups.

options.title: Fold into broader session breaker
options.body: Treat this issue as subagent evidence for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62615 and avoid a separate subagent-only policy surface.

recommendation.title: Design persisted session-health receipts
recommendation.body: Define failure signature, counter scope, last success, cooldown or half-open state, manual override, notification, and status output before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history on subagent registry/spawn boundaries and is the best available routing owner for the product contract choice.
